three_concepts: Human misunderstanding: open on a worker posing beside a generator. Filmer says “Just the generator”; worker says “Right” and steps aside. Payoff: the small awkward pause. Needs one natural performed take; risk: overacting.

Satisfying finishing detail: open on actual finishing action, follow it to completion, then reveal the matching installation. Needs safely captured action and documented same-job context; current stills cannot establish progression.

Useful observation: a presenter asks what an equipment photo actually proves, then explains that installed equipment alone does not establish an operating test. Needs an accurate original performance and photo permission; risk: another text lecture rather than entertainment.
response.selection: Develop the human misunderstanding. It changes the storytelling mechanism and needs only one new take. This is proposed staged dialogue, not an existing employee exchange or completed company job.

three_concepts: Voice-led contrast: open on A-before with C’s homeowner wish, match-cut to A-after, end on B. Payoff: the intended reading corner becomes visually understandable. Needs A/B/C; risk: overediting natural speech.

Visual discovery: open on B’s light detail, widen to A-after, briefly compare A-before. Payoff: discover where the detail belongs. Needs A/B; risk: detail reveals everything before the room adds meaning.
Direct comparison: open with aligned, labeled A-before/after side by side, expand after, finish on B. Payoff: immediate visible comparison. Needs A/B; risk: narrow images obscure the light on phones.
response.selection: Choose voice-led contrast. The authorized observation gives this particular transformation human meaning without an absent reaction or installation-action shot.
shot_linked_treatment: 0–2.2s, provisional: A-before, full portrait angle; small “Before” label. Start C: “We wanted a reading corner, not a waiting room.” Subtitle exact speech in short synchronized phrases. No logo opener.

2.2–6.7s: hard match-cut to A-after, same crop; label “After.” Finish C naturally, then hold the room. Align the cut to an actual phrase boundary; adjust timings after listening. Do not darken before or exaggerate after.
6.7–9.7s: B’s three-second finished detail with its clean room audio. No extra text, invented reaction, or closing sales panel.
response.sound: Authentic C, then quiet B ambience; no music or added electrical effects. Check levels and intelligibility after listening. Exact subtitles and before/after labels support muted viewing; check phone legibility and platform-safe placement.
response.caption: Fixture draft: “We wanted a reading corner, not a waiting room.” Same room. A different feel.
response.creative_review: Ready for production/review within the fixture. Opening intention pays off in the matching reveal; B adds concrete detail. Natural verified wording passes the specificity test. Each shot has a job; no montage filler. Organic footage/voice permission is supplied, but no music or paid-use rights are inferred. Omit prices, savings, credentials, location, outage/test claims. Text review only: actual footage, sound, privacy, captions, and export remain unreviewed.
